title: Stochastic Saturation Fuzzer: cross-node token throughput and p95 regression detection for TP/PP stacks
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build and run a stochastic saturation fuzzer to exercise multi-GPU distributed inference stacks (tensor parallel + pipeline parallel) with adversarial microburst/interference patterns. The goal is to find throughput and p95 latency regressions that do not show up under steady-state soak tests by introducing randomized sequence-length distributions, inter-request jitter, skewed KV-cache warmup, and targeted kernel corner cases. This ticket scopes the harness, metric extraction, regression detector, and an automated playbook for triage and rollback gating.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A reproducible harness (k8s job + runner) that can spin up TP/PP topologies across 1-8 nodes and run stochastic workloads with configurable seeds
2) Telemetry pipeline that emits tokens/sec, p95, p50, p99, tail-drop rate, and KV-cache hit ratio per node/replica to Datadog and a benchmark dashboard
3) A regression detector that raises alerts when p95 increases >10% with 95% confidence using EWMA + bootstrap and correlates with tokens/sec drops

4) Stress cases that trigger at least three distinct kernel-level regressions in local lab (examples: sequence-length mixing, rapid cold-start streams, interleaved long/short with high KV churn), documented with PRs and reproducer configs
5) Automated artifact: for any failing run, produce a minimal run config (seed + topology + request trace) that reproduces the anomaly >90% of the time locally
test_plan: Phase A: implement stochastic load generator and topology orchestrator. Phase B: integrate metrics exporters and build dashboard. Phase C: run fuzz campaigns across historical model versions and produce a regression matrix. Phase D: hook detector into canary gating and create rollback playbook. Each phase has a short and long run: short runs (10m) for quick feedback; long runs (3h) to expose slow drift and KV warmup effects.
instrumentation_notes:
- Use existing token-metering shim to emit per-request token counts.
- Export per-GPU kernel counters where available and align timeline using NTP/syncer.
- Tag metrics with topology labels: TP=<N>, PP=<M>, mesh_latency_ms, interconnect_type.
- Record raw request traces (headers + first 256 tokens) for failing seeds only to limit storage.
- Add a lightweight per-run checksum to validate KV cache warmup behavior.
implementation_tasks: T1: Implement stochastic request generator (variable seqlen, jitter distribution, prefix reuse probability)
T2: Extend cluster job spec to deploy TP/PP topologies with custom cross-node placement hints
T3: Wire telemetry to Datadog and create temp dashboard with drift heatmaps
T4: Implement regression-detector service (EWMA + bootstrap) and attach to CI pipeline
T5: Create reproducer extraction and archive flow to GCS for triage
T6: Run campaign across last 8 runtime builds and summarize anomalies
prelim_results: Initial short-run fuzz campaign (2025-02-25) found a consistent p95 blowup (~18%) on a 4-node TP=2 PP=2 configuration when mixing 8% long (>=2048) sequences into a short-sequence workload. Kernel traces suggest a suboptimal kernel choice at 512-1024 boundary. Logged reproducer and created PR #9186 to add more granular kernel-selection telemetry.
